source.title: Commentary Critical and Explanatory on the Whole Bible
source.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset and David Brown
source.edition: CCEL expanded electronic edition of the 1871 public-domain text

entries.text: 2. Before God all are on the same footing ( Pr 14:31; 17:5 ).

entries.heading: 3. are punished
entries.text: 3. are punished --that is, for their temerity; for the evil is not necessarily punitive, as the prudent might otherwise be its objects.

entries.heading: 4. humility and the fear of the Lord
entries.text: 4. humility and the fear of the Lord --are in apposition; one produces the other. On the results, compare Pr 3:16; 8:18 .

entries.heading: 5. he that . . . them
entries.text: 5. he that . . . them --Those who properly watch over their own souls are thus preserved from the dangers which attend the way of perverse men ( Pr 16:17 ).

entries.heading: 6. Train
entries.text: 6. Train --initiate, or early instruct. the way --literally, "his way," that selected for him in which he should go; for early training secures habitual walking in it.
7. The influence of wealth sets aside moral distinctions is implied, and, of course, disapproved (compare Pr 19:6; 21:14 , &c.).
8. (Compare Pr 11:18; Ps 109:16-20; Ga 6:7, 8 ). the rod . . . fail --His power to do evil will be destroyed.

entries.heading: 9. a bountiful eye
entries.text: 9. a bountiful eye --that is, a beneficent disposition. for he giveth . . . poor --His acts prove it.

entries.heading: 10. Cast out
entries.text: 10. Cast out --or drive away. Scorners foster strife by taunts and revilings.
11. (Compare Margin ). pureness of heart --and gentle, kind words win favor, even from kings.

entries.heading: 12. preserve
entries.text: 12. preserve --or guard. knowledge --its principles and possessors. overthroweth --utterly confounds and destroys the wicked.
13. Frivolous excuses satisfy the indolent man's conscience.

entries.heading: 14. The mouth
entries.text: 14. The mouth --or flattering speeches ( Pr 5:3; 7:5 ) ensnare man, as pits, beasts. God makes their own sin their punishment.

entries.heading: 15. is bound
entries.text: 15. is bound --or firmly fixed. Chastisement deters from crime and so leads to reformation of principle.
16. These two vices pertain to the same selfish feeling. Both are deservedly odious to God and incur punishment.

17. Here begins another division of the book, marked by those encouragements to the pursuit of wisdom, which are found in the earlier chapters. It will be observed that at Pr 22:22-24:12 , the proverbs are generally expressed in two verses instead of one (see Introduction ).
18. These lessons must be laid up in the mind, and fitted --or better, "fixed" in the lips so as to be ever ready.

entries.heading: 19. That . . . Lord
entries.text: 19. That . . . Lord --This is the design of the instruction.

entries.heading: 20. excellent things
entries.text: 20. excellent things --or probably of former times. counsels and knowledge --both advice and instruction.
21. Specially he desires to secure accuracy, so that his pupil may teach others.
22, 23. Here follow ten precepts of two verses each. Though men fail to defend the poor, God will ( Pr 17:5; Ps 12:5 ). in the gate --place of public gathering ( Job 5:4; Ps 69:12 ).

entries.heading: 25. a snare . . . soul
entries.text: 25. a snare . . . soul --The unsuspecting are often misled by bad company.

entries.heading: 27. should he take,
entries.text: 27. should he take, &c.--that is, the creditor.
28. (Compare Pr 23:10 ). Do not entrench on others ( De 19:14; 27:17 ).
29. Success rewards diligence ( Pr 10:4; 21:5 ).
